identity: Opening of a Dar al-Maʿārif 'المكتبة الخضراء للأطفال' children's book — 'الحصان الطيار في بلاد الأسرار' by Ahmed Naguib, tenth printing. Four front-matter lines, then the tale of King al-Nuʿmān son of King Ḥassān, who hears of a wonder found only in بلاد الأعاجيب, sends an officer up the mountain to the sorcerer (a magic carpet ride down to his hall), learns the wonder is the winged horse and that the road is impossible, and dispatches a hundred soldiers across the desert. Written in light rhymed prose (الجاه والسلطان / أشكال وألوان / على البال / مرتاح البال) with the narrator addressing the child reader directly ('لماذا؟', 'تعال معي', 'هيا بنا نذهب').
law: §E/§O as revised in batch 13 — anything written FOR CHILDREN is a short-unit register whatever its literary trappings, and the connective is where it cuts. Measured target ~12 tokens: 53 boundaries over 634 tokens, 49 of them in the 603-token body = 12.3 tokens/segment. Nineteen boundaries are free (the token before each of the 18 <NL> plus the final token); the other 34 come from a small, lexically visible set: full-form ولكن، ف + a new event verb، و + a new topic NP with its own predicate، fronted adverbials (ولما، وأخيرا، وإذا، وأحيانا) with the cut placed BEFORE them، and asyndetic new sentences (سار الجنود).
reasoning:
The controlling discriminator in this text is the one recovered entry 2 identified and batch 15 re-confirmed on doc_dc967c8520e9: **full-form ولكن CUTS, clitic ولكنه/ولكني WELDS.** This document contains nine ولكن of both kinds and getting them right is worth nine decisions on its own. CUT before the full form at @106، @238، @341، @380. WELD the clitic at @60 (ولكنه لم يكن سعيدا)، @90 (ولكني أريد)، @255 (ولكنه دخل)، @286 (ولكنه لم ير أحدا). The one place I overrode the clitic rule is @430 ليتكلم before ولكنه أحس السجادة: welding there would make a 25-token segment in a 12-token register, and the sentence is the exact twin of @341 'فتح الضابط فمه ليتكلم ‖ ولكن قبل أن ينطق', which takes the full form. Medium, and it is my least defensible cut.
@164 شيء before ولهذا أرسل النعمان: batch 15 has just taught me at the cost of a false cut that bare لذا WELDS as a trailing result adjunct. I cut here anyway, on the same reasoning batch 15 used to reconcile لكن — **the و is doing the work.** ولهذا opens a new actor and a new event (the king dispatching an officer) after a completed statement, and welding would give 28 tokens. Medium; if it is wrong, the rule is 'the whole لذا/ولذلك/ولهذا family welds', which I will then write down flat.
The §Y verb-counter from batch 14 is what governs the long journey paragraph @195-336: allow two coordinated verbs per segment and cut when a third arrives. That yields 'سار … حتى وصل ‖ ونظر … فرأى ‖ فأخذ يتسلق … ثم سار … حتى وصل ‖ فوقف … ورفع ‖' — twelve segments averaging 11.8 tokens, which is what this register should look like. I did NOT cut at @221 before ثم سار, because فأخذ + ثم سار is only the second verb of its segment.
Welds I defended: @290 أحدا before وإنما شعر — لم … وإنما is a single correlative ('not … but rather'), LAW 3's territory, not a boundary. @124-154, the 30-token 'إن الرجل الوحيد الذي كانوا يقولون … القريب من بلد الملك النعمان' — a chain of relatives with no available joint. @513-552, the 40-token dispatch order 'ثم نادى النعمان قائد جيشه وطلب منه أن يعد … وأن يرسل … ويأمرهم أن يعبروا … ثم يحضروا' — the longest segment in the document and syntactically forced: every clause after طلب is an أن-complement hanging off it. It is far over this register's norm and I accept it rather than cut inside a subordinate chain. G1 covers the speech at @342-359 and @450-458 likewise.
Rhymed prose: I cut @49 (أشكال وألوان) and @67 (مرتاح البال) on the rhyme, but only because each rhyme-unit is also a complete predication with its own topic (وعنده كل ما يخطر على البال). The rhyme is a corroborating signal, never the reason.
